workloads.name: pipeline
workloads.declared: GET /pipeline to the probe's configuration api, no request header of its own: a route that says unstaged and answers 2 bytes, the shortest request the probe answers, so the connection's code is the largest share of it. Touched: with the switch off a connection takes one more branch when it is accepted and a request takes the same path through hyper, but the compiled program is not the same (design Choice 78), so every request runs code this change compiles differently. Held to +1% with no floor; no reduction is declared.

workloads.name: get
workloads.declared: GET /baseline11?a=1&b=2 to the probe's configuration api, no request header of its own: a staged API route, typed query parameters in and a short answer out. Touched: with the switch off a connection takes one more branch when it is accepted and a request takes the same path through hyper, but the compiled program is not the same (design Choice 78), so every request runs code this change compiles differently. Held to +1% with no floor; no reduction is declared. Named for the catalog's json target: both are a staged API route's short answer through the same connection, service and router future, which is the code this change compiles differently.

workloads.name: page
workloads.declared: GET /page to the probe's configuration pages, no request header of its own: a staged page of about 12 KB, not compressed. Touched: with the switch off a connection takes one more branch when it is accepted and a request takes the same path through hyper, but the compiled program is not the same (design Choice 78), so every request runs code this change compiles differently. Held to +1% with no floor; no reduction is declared. Named for the catalog's page target: both are a staged page through the same connection, service and router future, which is the code this change compiles differently.

workloads.name: post
workloads.declared: POST /baseline11?a=1&b=2 with the 2-byte text/plain body 20 to the probe's configuration api (post.lua): a request with a body, which hyper reads. Touched: with the switch off a connection takes one more branch when it is accepted and a request takes the same path through hyper, but the compiled program is not the same (design Choice 78), so every request runs code this change compiles differently. Held to +1% with no floor; no reduction is declared. The kit captures the answers it compares with a GET, so the answers compared are those to a GET of this path; the POST's own answers are held only to wrk's count of failed requests, which must be zero in every turn.
